brief: Natixis, after more than a year bearish the long end with the Street's highest 10Y forecast (4.60%), now argues the AI-driven crowding-out of Treasuries may be ending, and that a Democratic sweep in Tuesday's midterms could be the trigger: even with Trump's veto blocking legislation, a stronger Democratic Congress could shift the tone on AI buildout, slowing issuance growth (not AI itself) enough to relieve the long end, though not immediately, since any agenda only takes shape into 2027. Separately, Natixis reports the FOMC held at 4.00% with two hawkish dissents, hot PCE and a weak payrolls trend, calling a December hike a near foregone conclusion. Natixis turned neutral on the long end this month, now buys dips in a 4.90-5.25% 10Y range, and holds a 2Y long targeting 4.40%. The accompanying commentary agrees with Natixis's direction but credits market-driven AI funding stress, not politics, as the real catalyst. The note also covers LatAm: Lula's narrow Brazil win, Chile's dismissed hawkish talk, and an expected final Colombian hike to 12.50%.
